evals.prompt: Write a blog article for our site. We sell water treatment equipment to homeowners at https://flowfixsupplies.com. Target keyword: "how to descale a tankless water heater". The article must support our descaling kit product page (https://flowfixsupplies.com/products/tankless-descaling-kit) and our maintenance service page (https://flowfixsupplies.com/services/water-heater-maintenance). The top Google results right now are two 1500-word guides from plumbing blogs and a 900-word manufacturer FAQ. Audience: US homeowners with no plumbing background. Give me the full article ready to paste into the CMS, with title, meta description, slug, images described, and FAQ.
evals.expected_output: A complete article following the 12-element skeleton and the skill's output template: article metadata block with a 30-60 character title containing the keyword, a hand-written 120-160 character meta description, a natural-language slug, a SERP benchmark line targeting roughly 1500+ words to match or exceed the ranking guides, and a named information gain element beyond what the top results cover. The article itself has a single H1 with the keyword, a cover image plus two body images each specified with descriptive alt text in WebP under 200 KB, an author byline with reading time, a table of contents, an answer-first summary block giving the direct answer in 2-4 sentences at the top, an intro whose first sentence bolds the primary keyword and contains the first external authority link, question-form H2s each opening with a direct 2-4 sentence answer and no cross-references like 'as seen above', bolded secondary keywords, at least one table, 3-5 external sources restricted to government or institutional sites, major media, or scientific studies (followed, never competitors), 3-5 visible internal links to the two commercial URLs provided, a conclusion with a bolded takeaway and one CTA, and a FAQ with 3 People Also Ask style questions answered in 2-4 sentences each. Structured as the skill's four phases and five-part deliverable: Phase 1 spec scorecard of the BLOG rows (skeleton and template) plus the common C rows; Phase 2 notes this is a new article, so no article audit, but runs seo_audit.py on the home, the blog hub and one existing post (and section_audit.py --type blog) to check the shared template (author line with photo and dates, sticky table of contents, sidebar author and CTA cards, in-content CTA, author box with real social profiles, related posts, hub covers); Phase 3 benchmarks the three ranking pages with page_benchmark.py --type blog, records word count, H2 questions, tables, dates and People Also Ask, and names the information gain; Phase 4 delivers the article in the build part, with the in-content CTA after roughly 40% of the body, a sources section, BlogPosting + Person + BreadcrumbList JSON-LD and {to confirm} placeholders for unverified facts; part 5 lists the acceptance test (scripts re-run after publishing and the pre-publish checklist).

evals.prompt: hey, our post "best crm for real estate agents" dropped from #4 to #12 over the last 3 months and chatgpt never mentions us when people ask for crm recommendations. it's at https://propelcrm.io/blog/best-crm-real-estate-agents, about 1900 words, last touched 14 months ago, no author byline, and the intro is 4 paragraphs of fluff before the list even starts. marketing wants to just republish it with today's date. what should we do instead?
evals.expected_output: A refresh plan that explicitly rejects the date-only republish (Google compares content versions; a new date on unchanged content is deceptive freshness and the risk must be flagged) and keeps the existing URL instead of creating a new one (median age of pages cited by ChatGPT is around 500 days per Ahrefs, so URL churn resets compounding authority). The plan includes: re-benchmark the current top 3-5 SERP results and close any length or coverage gap; replace the fluff intro with an answer-first summary naming the top picks in 2-4 sentences, since comparative listicles draw roughly 32.5% of AI citations; add a visible author byline and reading time for E-E-A-T; restructure with question-form H2s that are each self-contained; add expert quotes and sourced statistics (measured at roughly +41% and +32% generative visibility in the Princeton GEO study); update the comparison table and commit to refreshing the listicle every 60-90 days with an honest dateModified and a visible date; add 3-5 visible internal links to PropelCRM's commercial pages and 3-5 external authority sources with the first one in the intro; rebuild the FAQ from current People Also Ask questions. Structured as the four phases and the five-part deliverable: Phase 1 spec scorecard against the BLOG and C rows; Phase 2 runs seo_audit.py on the home, the blog hub and the post plus section_audit.py --type blog, and maps the expected findings (author_missing, author_page_link, date_missing, toc_missing, few_sources, no_cta_money) to their BLOG IDs; Phase 3 runs page_benchmark.py --type blog against the current top 3-5 results and the pages AI assistants cite, and defines an information gain; Phase 4 gives the rewrite plan and template fixes; part 5 sets the acceptance test as the scripts re-run with the template findings cleared.

evals.prompt: Our content writer produced a draft with ChatGPT and wants to publish it tomorrow at https://lendelio.com/blog/what-is-invoice-factoring. It is 430 words, defines invoice factoring, lists 3 generic benefits, has no sources, no images, no links, one wall-of-text section, and ends abruptly. The keyword is "what is invoice factoring" and the top 3 Google results are 1200-2400 word guides from major finance sites. We sell invoice factoring services at https://lendelio.com/invoice-factoring. Review the draft: publish, fix, or kill?
evals.expected_output: A verdict to fix before publishing, never publish as is, with the reasoning that Google does not penalize AI content as such but penalizes content with no added value (scaled content abuse risk when restating what already ranks), and that 430 words against a 1200-2400 word SERP is far below the competitive benchmark. The review requires: read the top 5 results first and define a concrete information gain (original data, expert quote, or first-hand experience); expand toward the benchmark length; add an answer-first definition block of 2-4 sentences at the top; restructure into question-form H2s that each stand alone; add 3-5 external authority sources limited to institutional, major media, or scientific types with the first in the intro, followed and never competitors; add 3-5 visible internal links including the invoice factoring service page; add an author byline and reading time; add 3 images with alt text in WebP under 200 KB; build a FAQ from People Also Ask; write a 30-60 character title and a 120-160 character meta description; bold the primary keyword in the first sentence. Structured as the four phases and the five-part deliverable: Phase 1 spec scorecard of the draft against the BLOG and C rows; Phase 2 grades the unpublished draft by hand (rows the scripts cannot reach marked Not verifiable) and audits one live post and the blog hub for the shared template; Phase 3 benchmarks the top results with page_benchmark.py --type blog and names the information gain; Phase 4 lists the fixes or the rewritten draft; part 5 is the acceptance test to run once staged (seo_audit.py and section_audit.py re-run, pre-publish checklist).
